entities.name: Evermode of Ratzeburg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Evermode of Ratzeburg (died 1178-02-24) emerged as a foundational figure in the Premonstratensian Order, a pivotal monastic movement of the 12th century, and a key agent in the Christianization and Germanization of the Polabian Slavs. As the lifelong companion of Norbert of Xanten, the order's founder, Evermode played an indispensable role in establishing its early structure and expanding its influence, particularly into the nascent ecclesiastical territories east of the Elbe River. His appointment as the first Premonstratensian Bishop of Ratzeburg placed him at the vanguard of the *Drang nach Osten*, a sustained push by German secular and ecclesiastical powers into Slavic lands, profoundly shaping the religious and political landscape of Nordalbingia.

Born in Brabant (modern Belgium), Evermode joined Norbert's nascent community at Prémontré in 1120, becoming one of its earliest canons regular. He accompanied Norbert to Rome in 1125 to secure papal confirmation for the order and was instrumental in its initial administration and expansion. Following Norbert's death in 1134, Evermode continued to serve the order, eventually becoming abbot of Gottesgnaden. In 1154, Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony, appointed him Bishop of Ratzeburg, a crucial frontier diocese. During his episcopate until 1178, Evermode vigorously promoted the conversion of the Wends, establishing new parishes, fostering German settlement, and rebuilding Ratzeburg Cathedral, which he consecrated in 1170 after its destruction in 1154.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Evermode of Ratzeburg played a crucial role in the expansion of the Premonstratensian Order and the Christianization of the Polabian Slavs, contributing significantly to the cultural and political integration of Nordalbingia into the Holy Roman Empire.
